# Third review of SEEN-108, attempt 5, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned fresh on opus with the task text of triage record 57. Verdict `return`,
six findings. It confirmed the five criteria met as worded, settled the three
partly-settled checks by comparison, and judged `slice_files` a plan-accuracy
gap rather than a defect, on the same reasoning the first review gave.

On Ruud's decision, F1 and F2 are fixed in this ticket and F3 to F6 go to a
follow-up. All six are recorded here in full so the follow-up quotes evidence
rather than a summary.

## Fixed here

- **F1, high, harness/agents/seen-implementer.md:23 with routing.py:292 and
  skill.md:63.** Nothing tells the implementer subagent to pass `harness check
  --model <tier>`, so the declaration the amended criterion 3 rests on is never
  made and the gate always falls back to the session log, which reports the
  parent's model. Confirmed: `--model` appears in exactly two places in the
  repository, the parser and a test fixture. With shadow off, a subagent spawned
  on haiku for a slice routed to haiku runs check exactly as instructed, records
  model claude-opus-5 and model_declared None, and the gate refuses a slice that
  ran exactly as routed. That is the defect record 50 amended the criterion to
  prevent: the gate's half landed and the instruction half did not.
- **F2, medium, harness/kpi.py:163.** `_closes` keys a tdd advance's window at
  `last + 1` with no bound, so the second and every later tdd advance of a
  reworked ticket closes a position that does not exist and its tokens are
  dropped, which makes a reworked route look cheaper in the table SEEN-109
  decides from. On this ticket's own journal the same mechanism runs slice 4's
  window from record 17 to record 56, swallowing all four review rounds:
  253,085 output tokens and 1,898 cents charged to a 2-point slice, 62 per cent
  of the ticket. repowise puts kpi.py at a 93 per cent hotspot score with an
  increasing trend.

## Carried to the follow-up

- **F3, medium, harness/tests/test_agents.py:122.**
  `test_an_agent_file_nobody_generates_is_reported` and
  `test_a_stray_codex_agent_file_is_reported_too` now pass through `drift()`
  rather than `strays()`, because seen-implementer became a generated agent and
  its name is in the `generated` set. Delete `+ strays(root)` from `agents.drift`
  and both stay green. The behaviour they guarded is F10 of SEEN-105's first
  review: an agent file with no source under harness/agents/, holding Edit,
  Write and Bash, that nobody reviewed.
- **F4, low, record 38.** The accepted tdd record of attempt 3 quotes
  "AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'ran_on_tier'"; check 34
  contains `KeyError: 'ran_on_tier'` and no AttributeError. The third instance of
  the fault notes 42 and 52 corrected for records 23 and 46, and the only one
  still uncorrected. The remedy is a correcting note.
- **F5, low, harness/report.py:184.** The rendered cost table tells its reader
  the routed counterfactual is "compared by `report --calibration`", a command
  that does not exist until SEEN-109. context.py says "which is SEEN-109's"
  beside the same sentence and the rendered prose drops the attribution.
- **F6, low, harness/thresholds.toml:177.** `money = ["packages/core/src/*"]` is
  an fnmatch pattern, so a slice whose files entry names `packages/core` or
  `packages/core/src` escapes the rule and can be routed to haiku at low effort
  for fee expectations or matching. No slice plan in any journal here names a
  directory today, so it is latent rather than live.
- **Not a finding, carried anyway.** `harness/cli.py` `go_back` assigns the
  record to a local and returns it with no behaviour change, a leftover from the
  sync that moved to the solution advance.
